Skin Doctor-led

Chemical Peel Treatment

A chemical peel is one of the quickest ways to get clearer, brighter skin. At Facelit, our doctors pick the acid and strength that suit your skin, whether you are dealing with acne, pigmentation, tan, open pores or the first fine lines. Most sessions take under an hour, and many peels need no downtime at all.

30–45 minPer session
0–7 daysDowntime
4–6Sessions typical
2–4 weeksBetween sessions
Book Now Explore our peels
On this page OverviewConcernsOur peelsProcessResultsAftercareCompareFAQs

Treatment overview

What is a Chemical Peel?

A chemical peel treatment uses a mild, carefully chosen acid to remove the top layer of dull, damaged skin. Your doctor brushes it on, leaves it for a few minutes, then neutralises it. Over the next few days the old cells shed, and the fresher skin underneath comes through. The peel also nudges your skin to make new collagen, which is why texture keeps improving after each session.

Scrubs and home exfoliants only polish the surface. A professional peel works evenly and goes a little deeper, so it can fade acne marks, soften scars and even out pigmentation in a way your daily routine usually can't.

Read more: the acids we use

We tailor every peel to your skin type, your main concern and your skin tone, which matters a lot for Indian skin. Depending on what you want to fix, your doctor may use:

  • AHAs (glycolic, lactic, mandelic): smooth and brighten the surface.
  • BHA (salicylic acid): dissolves oil inside the pores, so it suits acne-prone skin.
  • TCA (trichloroacetic acid): a stronger acid for scars, wrinkles and sun damage.
  • Retinoid peels (yellow peel): speeds up cell turnover to fade pigmentation.
  • Depigmenting systems (Cosmelan, Dermamelan): calm down the excess melanin behind melasma.

Peels work well on their own, and they also pair nicely with microneedling, laser or HydraFacial when you want faster results. Want to learn more? Read what medi-peels are.

SuperficialWorks on the outer layer. Good for glow, mild acne and tan.
MediumReaches a little deeper for pigmentation, melasma and fine lines.
TargetedApplied only on stubborn scars and deep texture.

What to expect

Benefits of Chemical Peel Treatment

A good course of peels does more than one job. Here is what most of our clients notice.

Brighter Skin

Takes away that tired, flat look and brings back clarity and colour.

Radiant Complexion

Encourages new cells and collagen, so skin looks healthy rather than shiny.

Even Skin Tone

Fades tan, dark spots and patchy pigmentation.

Beats Dry Skin

Clears flaky build-up, so your moisturiser actually sinks in.

Pimples, Goodbye!

Unclogs pores, calms active acne and cuts down new breakouts.

Smoother Scars

Softens acne scars and rough texture session by session.

Refined Pores

Clears oil from pores so they look smaller and tighter.

Younger-looking Skin

Softens fine lines and age spots for fresher-looking skin.

Swipe to see more

Is it right for you?

Skin Problems a Chemical Peel Can Treat

Tap a concern to see how a peel helps, which peels we usually recommend and roughly how many sessions it takes.

Active acne & breakouts

Acne starts when oil, dead skin and bacteria get trapped in a pore. A chemical peel for acne, usually salicylic or mandelic acid, breaks up that blockage from inside, settles the redness and means fewer new pimples. Your regular acne creams also tend to work better once the skin is clear of build-up.

  • Clears blackheads and whiteheads
  • Controls excess oil
  • Reduces red, inflamed spots
Recommended peelsSalicylic Acid PeelMandelic Acid Peel360 Combination Peel
Typical sessions4–6, every 2 weeks
Types of acne explained

Acne scars & post-acne marks

The brown or red marks pimples leave behind respond quickly to light peels. Pitted scars, like ice-pick or boxcar scars, are tougher. For those we use targeted TCA, often alongside microneedling or laser, and results build over several months.

  • Fades brown and red post-acne marks
  • Softens shallow scars
  • Smooths uneven texture
Recommended peelsFerulac PeelTCA PeelMandelic Acid Peel
Typical sessions4–6, every 3–4 weeks
Acne scar treatment

Pigmentation & melasma

Melasma and long-standing dark patches need more than exfoliation. Depigmenting peels such as Cosmelan and Dermamelan slow down the skin's extra melanin while lifting the pigment that's already there. Daily sunscreen is what keeps it from coming back.

  • Lightens melasma and hormonal patches
  • Evens out blotchy skin tone
  • Paired with a home skincare plan
Recommended peelsCosmelan PeelDermamelan PeelYellow Peel
Typical sessions1–4, with home maintenance
Peels for pigmentation

Sun tan & uneven tone

The Kerala sun is tough on skin, and tan builds up fast. Brightening peels lift the tanned outer layer and bring back your natural tone. Many people see a difference after the very first session.

  • Removes tan from face, neck and arms
  • Brightens dull, sun-exposed skin
  • Little to no downtime
Recommended peelsGlycolic Acid PeelPumpkin PeelVitamin C Peel
Typical sessions2–4, every 2 weeks
How to remove tan

Dull, dehydrated skin

Stress, pollution and late nights leave a layer of dead cells that makes skin look flat. A gentle glow peel clears it away, so your skin catches the light again and feels softer. It's a favourite before weddings and big events.

  • Instant glow with no downtime
  • Smoother makeup application
  • Great pre-event treatment
Recommended peelsParty PeelVitamin C PeelPumpkin Peel
Typical sessions1–3, as needed
Skin glow treatments

Open pores & oily skin

Pores look bigger when oil and debris stretch them out. Oil-dissolving peels clean them from the inside and tighten the surface, so pores look smaller and your skin stays less shiny through the day.

  • Visibly smaller-looking pores
  • Less oil and shine
  • Fewer blackheads
Recommended peelsSalicylic Acid PeelGlycolic Acid Peel360 Combination Peel
Typical sessions4–6, every 2–3 weeks
Book a pore consultation

Fine lines & sun damage

Years of sun leave behind age spots, rough patches and early wrinkles. Peels speed up cell renewal and boost collagen, which softens fine lines and fades sun spots over a few sessions.

  • Fades age and sun spots
  • Softens fine lines
  • Improves firmness and texture
Recommended peelsGlycolic Acid PeelVitamin C PeelTCA Peel
Typical sessions4–6, every 3–4 weeks
Anti-ageing treatments
Also treats: Dark underarms & neckBack & body acneDark knees & elbowsRough, bumpy skinPre-bridal glowRazor bumps

Types of chemical peels

Superficial, Medium and Targeted Peels

Peels are grouped by how deep they work. Your doctor decides the strength after looking at your skin, and stronger is not always better.

Superficial Peel

Gentle acids like glycolic, lactic, mandelic and salicylic. A good starting point for glow and mild concerns.

Best for: dullness, tan, mild acne, oily skin
Downtime: none to 2 days of mild flaking
Sessions: 4–6, every 2–3 weeks

Medium Peel

Blends such as TCA, Cosmelan and Dermamelan for concerns that sit a little deeper.

Best for: pigmentation, melasma, acne marks, fine lines
Downtime: 3–7 days of peeling
Sessions: 1–4, spaced 3–4 weeks

Targeted Peel

A stronger acid dabbed only onto specific scars (for example TCA CROSS), never across the whole face.

Best for: ice-pick and boxcar acne scars
Downtime: 5–7 days on treated spots
Sessions: 3–5, every 4–6 weeks

Your appointment

Chemical Peel Procedure: Step by Step

A little preparation goes a long way. It makes your peel safer and the results better.

  • Your doctor assesses your skin type, tone and texture to recommend the right peel.
  • Tell your doctor about any allergies (including glycolic acid), medicines or recent treatments.
  • A patch test checks how your skin reacts to the chosen solution.
  • Avoid waxing, bleaching and threading on the area for a week before.
  • Stop scrubs, retinoids and benzoyl peroxide products 48–72 hours before.
  • Some peels need 2–4 weeks of priming creams to prepare the skin.

The whole session takes 30 to 45 minutes, and you can go straight back to your day.

  • The skin is cleansed and degreased; sensitive areas like eyes and lips are protected.
  • The peel solution is applied evenly with a brush.
  • It stays on for about 3–5 minutes depending on the formula. You may feel a mild tingle, which is normal.
  • A neutralising solution is used to stop the peel at the right time.
  • Cool compresses soothe the skin, followed by a hydrating cream and sunscreen.

How you look after your skin now decides how good the results are. The full aftercare plan is below.

  • Avoid direct sun and heat (saunas, steam, hot yoga) while the skin heals.
  • Apply broad-spectrum SPF 30+ sunscreen and reapply through the day.
  • Don't pick or scratch flaking skin. Let it shed naturally.
  • Skip waxing, threading or bleaching on the area for one week.
  • Avoid Retin-A and other strong actives for at least 72 hours.
  • Keep skin well moisturised with a gentle, fragrance-free cream.

Recovery & results

Chemical Peel Results and Recovery

Every peel is a little different, but this is what most people go through after a light to medium peel.

  1. Day 0–2

    Tight & pink

    Skin may feel tight, warm or a little red, a bit like mild sunburn.

  2. Day 3–7

    Gentle peeling

    Light flaking as old cells shed. Moisturise and let it come off naturally.

  3. Week 2

    Fresh glow

    New skin looks brighter, smoother and more even.

  4. After 4–6 sessions

    Lasting change

    Visible fading of marks, pigmentation and texture, maintained with good skincare.

Aftercare

Chemical Peel Aftercare

Follow this simple plan to heal faster and keep your results for longer.

Do

  • Wash with a mild, soap-free cleanser and lukewarm water
  • Apply the moisturiser your doctor recommends 2–3 times a day
  • Use SPF 30+ sunscreen, even indoors
  • Sleep on a clean pillowcase

Avoid

  • Makeup for the first 24 hours
  • Hot showers, steam, saunas and heavy workouts
  • Scrubs, retinol, AHAs or vitamin C serums
  • Touching, picking or rubbing your skin

Do

  • Keep moisturising generously. Flaking is normal
  • Gently pat skin dry after washing
  • Reapply sunscreen every 2–3 hours outdoors
  • Drink plenty of water

Avoid

  • Pulling off flakes. Let them shed on their own
  • Swimming in chlorinated pools
  • Waxing, threading or bleaching
  • Direct midday sun

Morning routine

  • Gentle cleanser
  • Brightening serum, once your doctor says it's fine
  • Light moisturiser
  • Broad-spectrum SPF 30–50

Night routine

  • Gentle cleanser
  • Treatment cream prescribed for your concern
  • Barrier-repair moisturiser
  • Maintenance peel every 1–3 months

Your skin type

Which Peel Suits Your Skin Type?

Oily & acne-prone skin
Salicylic and mandelic peels clean out pores and keep oil in check. Most people see fewer breakouts and smaller-looking pores within a few sessions.
Dry skin
Lactic acid and Vitamin C peels exfoliate gently and help skin hold on to moisture. We pair them with a rich barrier-repair cream.
Sensitive skin
We start with low-strength mandelic or pumpkin enzyme peels and a patch test, then increase gradually only if your skin is comfortable.
Combination skin
Your doctor may use a slightly stronger peel on an oily T-zone and a gentler one on drier cheeks.
Darker / Indian skin tones
We use slow-acting acids, careful timing and a few weeks of skin priming beforehand. That keeps the risk of post-peel darkening low without holding back on results.

Why Facelit

Why Choose Facelit for Chemical Peels in Kerala?

  1. 01

    Doctor-led consultation

    Every treatment starts with a proper skin check. Our doctors then build a plan around what bothers you most, whether that's acne, pigmentation, fine lines or dullness.

  2. 02

    Peels customised for Indian skin

    Indian skin can darken if a peel is too strong. We pick the acid, strength and timing for your skin tone to keep that risk low.

  3. 03

    Medical-grade formulations

    We only use professional, clinically tested peels, from gentle glow peels to depigmentation systems like Cosmelan and Dermamelan.

  4. 04

    Safe, hygienic and comfortable

    You are treated in a clean, calm clinic with strict hygiene standards, and we soothe your skin properly before you leave.

  5. 05

    Aftercare and follow-up

    You leave with a clear aftercare routine, and we check your progress at every visit so the plan keeps up with your skin.

Safety first

Chemical Peel Side Effects and Who Should Wait

In trained hands, chemical peels are very safe. Here is what is normal afterwards, and when it is better to wait.

Common and temporary

  • Mild redness or warmth for a few hours to 2 days
  • Light flaking or peeling for 3–7 days
  • Tightness or dryness, which moisturiser eases
  • Temporary sensitivity to sun and strong products

Talk to your doctor first if you

  • Are pregnant or breastfeeding
  • Have taken oral isotretinoin in the last 6 months
  • Have active cold sores, infections, cuts or eczema on the area
  • Have a fresh sunburn or recent tan
  • Tend to form keloids or raised scars

Questions

Chemical Peel FAQs

Does a chemical peel hurt?
Not really. Most people feel a mild tingle or warmth for a few minutes while the peel is on. We use cool compresses and a soothing cream straight after, so you leave comfortable.
How many chemical peel sessions will I need?
Most concerns need 4–6 sessions spaced 2–4 weeks apart. A glow peel before an event may need just one, while melasma or acne scars usually need a full course. Your doctor will recommend a plan after your consultation.
Is there any downtime after a chemical peel?
Light peels have little or no downtime, and most people go back to work the same day. Medium peels can cause visible peeling for 3 to 7 days. We'll tell you exactly what to expect beforehand so you can plan around it.
Are chemical peels safe for Indian and darker skin tones?
Yes, when the right peel is chosen. We use formulas such as mandelic, lactic and depigmenting peels that are suited to darker skin, and adjust strength and timing to reduce the risk of irritation or post-peel darkening.
When will I see results?
Many people notice brighter, smoother skin within 1–2 weeks of the first session. Improvements in pigmentation, acne marks and texture build up with each session and are most visible after a full course.
How long do chemical peel results last?
Results can last for months when you protect your skin with daily sunscreen and a good skincare routine. Maintenance peels every 1–3 months help keep the results going.
Can I wear makeup after a chemical peel?
It is best to avoid makeup for at least 24 hours after a superficial peel, and until peeling stops after a medium peel, to let the skin heal and avoid irritation.
Can I go out in the sun after a peel?
Avoid direct sun for at least a week. If you must go out, wear SPF 30+ sunscreen, reapply every 2–3 hours, and use a hat or umbrella. Sun exposure on freshly peeled skin can cause dark patches.
Can I get a chemical peel before my wedding?
Yes. A series of glow peels is a popular part of bridal skin prep. Start 2–3 months before the wedding and schedule your last peel 7–10 days before the big day so there is no visible flaking.
Where can I get a chemical peel in Kerala?
Facelit offers chemical peel treatment at our clinics in Kowdiar (Trivandrum), Karunagappally (Kollam) and Guruvayur (Thrissur). You can book online or call your nearest clinic.
Can chemical peels be combined with other treatments?
Yes. Peels are often paired with microneedling, MNRF, laser or HydraFacial for better results on acne scars and pigmentation. Your doctor will space the treatments safely.
Can men get chemical peels?
Absolutely. Peels work just as well for men, especially for acne, oily skin, open pores, razor bumps and tan.
What is the difference between a chemical peel and a facial?
A facial cleanses and hydrates the surface of the skin. A chemical peel is a medical treatment that exfoliates deeper and stimulates skin renewal, so it treats concerns like acne, scars and pigmentation more effectively.
How much does a chemical peel cost?
Chemical peel cost depends on the type of peel, the area treated and how many sessions you need. Book a consultation for a personalised quote, or read our guide to the cost of peels in Trivandrum.
